source: Agriculture Sector Development Project (ASDP), ADB Loan No. 2023-CAM(SF), Guide No.1: Coconut-damaging beetle and protective measures, prepared by Kampot Province Department of Agricultural Extension, 2008
text:
The coconut-damaging beetle described in this guide is a hispine leaf beetle, shown in the guide as a slender, dark, winged adult insect roughly 1-1.6 cm long with a reddish-orange thorax marking.

The beetle has four life stages: egg (ពង, about 5 days), larva (ដង្កូវ, about 30 days, with the larva passing through four instars visibly darkening and lengthening from a pale cream color at day 5 to a dark reddish-purple color by around day 15), pupa (ដីកខ្យើ, about 7 days), and adult beetle (ខ្ជូងពេញវ័យ, living roughly 180-220 days).

An adult female can lay 2 to 5 eggs per day, and over her lifetime a single female may lay approximately 150 to 400 eggs, with total egg output depending on food availability. Both larvae and adults feed on young, still-unopened leaves. The guide notes the beetle's host range is not limited to coconut: it also attacks sugar palm (ស្លឹកដូងស្រាយ / ត្នោត), Cycas (ពួកអំបូរ Cycas), and other palm-family plants, meaning nearby sugar palm or ornamental Cycas plantings can serve as alternate hosts or reservoirs for reinfestation.
